problem:
Given that 
$|\begin{aligned}a+2 & -2 & 2 \\ b+3 & 4 & 2 \\ c & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|=5,$
find 
$|\begin{aligned}a+1 & -2 & 2 \\ b & 4 & 2 \\ c & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|.$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using the Linearity of the Determinant
examples.worked_solution:
We "factor out" the given determinant from the determinant we would like to find:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}a & b & c+1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}a+0 & b+0 & c+1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the linearity property of determinants and expanding the second determinant across the $1$st row, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}a+0 & b+0 & c+1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & ={{|\begin{aligned}a & b & c \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|}_{⏟}}_{-10}+|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-10+1(-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-10-1 \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Given an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ we have

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}.
$$

First, we find $|A|$ using a Laplace expansion across the $2$nd column:

$$
\begin{aligned}|A| & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & -2 \\ -6 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}|+1(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}|-2(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(12-12)+(-15+24)+2(10-16) \\  & =0+9-12 \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$
